themes_detail.label: Lot Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Lot condition complaints surged to 3 this week versus a baseline of 0.4 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 700% spike (z-score: 5.42)—signaling possible rapid deterioration of vacant properties or open spaces across Far Rockaway that residents are reporting at unprecedented rates.
evidence: 3 lot condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Highest statistical anomaly in the dataset, indicating sudden, concentrated outbreak
Correlates with 405 DOB permits filed in last 90 days (143 new buildings), suggesting construction disruption or site abandonment
reporting_angles: On-the-ground inspection of vacant lots in Far Rockaway to identify what residents are reporting—are lots attracting debris, illegal dumping, or safety hazards?

Interview residents and community board about whether lot deterioration is tied to stalled development projects (Edgemere Commons, Arverne East, 14-10 Beach Channel Drive all in active review/modification)

themes_detail.label: Flooring & Stairs Safety Spike
themes_detail.summary: Flooring and stairs complaints jumped to 15 last week versus a baseline of 5.5 per week—a 173% spike (z-score: 4.25)—suggesting a possible wave of interior structural or safety code violations affecting residential buildings across the district.
evidence: 15 flooring/stairs complaints last week vs. 5.5 weekly average over 8 weeks (173% spike, z-score: 4.25)
Second-most acute spike in dataset; directly affects tenant safety and habitability
Aligns with ongoing plumbing (417 total complaints, 8th highest) and general construction complaints (71% up 3 weeks ago)
reporting_angles: Interview tenants in buildings with filed complaints about whether landlords are making repairs or if complaints are being ignored
Cross-check DOB alteration permits (228 filed) against flooring complaint addresses to determine if repairs are being properly licensed or if slum conditions are worsening

themes_detail.label: Root/Sewer Infrastructure Failure
themes_detail.summary: Root and sewer complaints surged to 6 last week versus a baseline of 1.0 per week—a 500% spike (z-score: 3.78)—indicating acute underground infrastructure damage affecting streets and properties; this aligns with longstanding CB budget requests for sanitary sewer capital projects.
evidence: 6 root/sewer/sidewalk complaints last week vs. 1.0 weekly average (500% spike, z-score: 3.78)
Systemic issue: Community Board has repeatedly requested DEP capital funding to 'develop a capital project for specific street segments currently lacking sanitary sewers'
Converges with street condition complaints (962 total, 5th highest volume) and plumbing complaints (417 total)
reporting_angles: Investigate which streets are reporting root/sewer damage and cross-check against DEP infrastructure age maps—are certain blocks systematically underfunded?
Interview DEP about timeline for the 'planned capital project' mentioned in CB budget requests; what is blocking sewer upgrades in Far Rockaway?

themes_detail.label: Dangling Street Signs & Public Safety
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints jumped to 9 three weeks ago versus a baseline of 3.2 per week—a 177% spike (z-score: 3.22)—indicating possible weather damage, deferred maintenance, or enforcement lapses that could pose navigational and safety risks to residents and drivers.
evidence: 9 dangling street sign complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 3.2 weekly average (177% spike, z-score: 3.22)
Correlates with snow/ice (1101 complaints) and general street condition issues (962 complaints), suggesting weather-driven infrastructure decline
Sign of broader deferred maintenance across public right-of-way
reporting_angles: Visual survey of Far Rockaway streets to document dangling, missing, or illegible signs; photograph and map affected intersections
Contact DOT about complaint response times and maintenance schedules for signage in this district

themes_detail.label: Non-Emergency Police Call Surge
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police complaints reached 12 three weeks ago versus a baseline of 2.6 per week—a 357% spike (z-score: 3.43)—suggesting a spike in quality-of-life or minor crime complaints that may reflect either increased resident reporting or an emerging pattern of low-level incidents.
evidence: 12 non-emergency police complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 2.6 weekly average (357% spike, z-score: 3.43)
Correlates with Emergency Response Team spike (380% up, 3 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.6 avg)
Timing suggests a concentrated incident cluster rather than sustained trend; current status unclear
reporting_angles: NYPD incident data: Drill into what types of non-emergency complaints spiked 3 weeks ago—noise, trespassing, suspicious activity, etc.
Community interviews about safety concerns and whether residents feel conditions have changed
